done.why: I read enough to judge the writing after a short wander. I stopped early and did not push toward any ending.

about: A Zork-style underground empire. You arrive as a veteran adventurer after a dream in which an old silver-haired man says you face a final test. You start at the foot of an endless stair, with your old brass lantern, and explore dark passages, a sword stuck in a rock, and a sunlit cliff oasis.

moments.note: The lantern description reads like an old friend, with personality.
The sword's hilt turns out to be worn to the shape of your own hand.
The Cliff oasis, with giant trees under a sunlit hole, is vivid.
The room text mentions something 'not a tree' keeping still, but I could not examine it by that name.
Moving south put me in the dark, with the classic grue warning.

wished: To examine the hidden still thing among the trees
To read the runes on the sword
To work out what the final test is

lines.line: a hilt worn to the shape of a hand, which, when you close yours on it, turns out to be yours.
lines.why: A small, intimate detail that works well.

lines.line: It has the look of an old friend who has followed you somewhere it would rather not have come.
lines.why: It gives the lantern character and dry humour.

lines.line: Somebody left it under the tree not long ago, and did not come back for it, or has not yet.
lines.why: It implies another presence in the world.

fun.why: Pleasant, with careful touches, though I played only briefly.

engagement.why: The hints of another presence and a final test make me want to continue.

difficulty.why: I saw little challenge in this short run.

interestingness.why: It builds on a familiar Zork setting with new mysteries.

prose.why: The object descriptions are specific, wry and evocative.
